claims.statement: oxyromon is a cross-platform Rust CLI ROM organizer that validates ROM files against Logiqx DAT catalogs (No-Intro, Redump, MAME/FBNeo), imports them into a managed directory tree, sorts by region/1G1R preference and converts/exports between formats; the same binary optionally serves a GraphQL API with an embedded web UI and the Model Context Protocol, both behind Cargo features and both reusing the CLI subcommand implementations rather than reimplementing them.

The shortest working path is `cargo build --release` for the CLI, which has no special requirements; adding `--features server` additionally builds the Leptos web UI and therefore requires the Trunk bundler and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target.

The canonical user loop is import-dats (creating the system) -> import-roms (matching and placing files in the system's base directory) -> sort-roms (distributing files across the system directory, 1G1R and Trash); a system must already exist in the database for ROMs to match, and sorting requires at least one region configured in REGIONS_ALL or REGIONS_ONE.

On startup main.rs resolves a data directory (OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY, else the platform data dir plus `oxyromon`), creates the directory and `oxyromon.db` if missing, and opens the pool, which applies the compile-time embedded sqlx migrations automatically.

ROM_DIRECTORY (default ~/Emulation) and TMP_DIRECTORY (default system temp dir) are ordinary settings rows seeded lazily on first read from OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY / OXYROMON_TMP_DIRECTORY or the platform default and then persisted, so subsequent changes belong in the database rather than the environment; main.rs reads both at startup to guarantee they are initialized.

Configuration is stored in the SQLite settings table rather than a config file and is managed through the `config` subcommand; operations are global by default and `-n/--system` scopes them to a system, whose value takes precedence with automatic fallback to the global one.

The Cargo workspace is the root oxyromon package plus `crates/*` — seven format crates (`chd-rs`, `cia-rs`, `gdi-rs`, `nsz-rs`, `xdelta-rs`, `xps-rs`, `xso-rs`) — each also building a standalone CLI (`chdrs`, `ciars`, `gdirs`, `nszrs`, `xdeltars`, `xpsrs`, `xsors`) that `dist.sh` cross-builds and ships alongside oxyromon; `frontend/` and `desktop/` are deliberately not members, each declaring its own empty `[workspace]` so WebAssembly and Tauri/webview dependencies stay out of the native build.

build.rs shells out to `trunk build --release` in `frontend/` only when the `server` feature is enabled and SKIP_TRUNK is not `true`, and always creates `target/assets` so rust-embed compiles even with no UI built; the desktop app bundles the same `oxyromon` binary as a Tauri sidecar.

oxyromon runs no external program at runtime: CHD, CIA, GDI, NSZ, XDELTA, IPS/BPS and CSO/ZSO run in process through the `crates/` crates, archives through sevenz-rust2/zip and RVZ/WBFS through nod. `oxyromon info` lists every backend's `get_version()`, each printing `built-in`, with NSZ special-cased to `built-in, prod.keys not found` because only compressing NCAs needs keys.

Repo-wide invariant: romfile paths are stored relative to ROM_DIRECTORY, so writers must strip the prefix and readers must join it; CommonRomfile::get_relative_path does the strip and errors when a path lies outside the ROM directory.

Repo-wide invariant: user-facing output goes through the progress.rs categorized print_* helpers (header, subheader, info, success, warning, error, skip, action, separator) bound to a process-wide `MultiProgress`, and stdout must never be written directly from a path the MCP server can reach because `oxyromon mcp` (and the `/mcp` mount) carries JSON-RPC there — logs and progress go to stderr.

Repo-wide invariant: every new feature or notable change must update README.md (keeping each subcommand's usage block in sync with --help) and add a CHANGELOG.md entry under the current version's section, for CLI, server, and bug-fix changes alike.

Every capability is exposed as one module implementing `pub fn subcommand() -> Command` plus `pub async fn main(connection, matches, progress_bar)`, registered in main.rs; because subcommand() is pure argv declaration, the GraphQL mutations and MCP tools reach the same code by synthesizing ArgMatches, so functionality implemented outside that contract is invisible to those surfaces.

Batch subcommands run inside a block holding the single pooled connection, while the feature-gated `mcp` and `server` dispatches are handled after that block with a cloned pool so they can keep serving, and `optimize_database` runs on the pool afterwards.
Because sqlx queries are compile-time verified against offline data, changing a query or adding a migration requires regenerating `.sqlx/` with `cargo sqlx prepare -- --features server`.

The workspace is validated with `cargo test --workspace --features oxyromon/server` (the package-qualified feature name is required because a workspace selection spans packages), and `test.sh` is exactly `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server --lcov --output-path lcov.info` with no extra flags; CI runs clippy with `--all-targets --features oxyromon/server` plus a second clippy pass with `--no-default-features --features use-rustls,mcp` so the stdio-only MCP build stays covered.

Feature gates as declared in Cargo.toml: default is `use-rustls`, and `server` implies `mcp` (plus the Streamable HTTP transport) so `oxyromon server` nests the same MCP handler at `/mcp`, while `mcp` alone builds only the stdio server; the SQLite pool follows the same gate — 5 connections with NORMAL locking when `server` or `mcp` is compiled in, otherwise a single connection with EXCLUSIVE locking.

Format modules do not spawn processes: `src/chd.rs`, `cia.rs`, `archive.rs`, `nsz.rs`, `xso.rs`, `xdelta.rs`, `xps.rs` and `rvz.rs` call their linked crate and return `"built-in"` from `get_version()`; `src/chdman.rs` and `src/ctrtool.rs` no longer exist.

`build.rs` runs `trunk build --release` in `frontend/` only when the `server` feature is on and `SKIP_TRUNK` is not `true`, asserting with an explicit message when `frontend/` is absent (as in the crates.io tarball) rather than blaming a missing trunk, and always creating `target/assets/` so rust-embed compiles with no UI built.

Region settings can be supplied per run instead of per database: `sort-roms` reads `REGIONS_ALL`/`REGIONS_ONE` from `--regions`/`--one-regions` argv when present and otherwise from the settings table, while arcade placement uses the separate `REGIONS_ALL_ARCADE`/`REGIONS_ONE_ARCADE` lists.
Sorting and the 1G1R election have their own workflow page, and sort-roms takes its regions per run from -r/--regions and -o/--1g1r, overriding REGIONS_ALL and REGIONS_ONE.
